newsitem.title: USA: Sportmart to take Q4 charge to exit Canada.
newsitem.headline: Sportmart to take Q4 charge to exit Canada.

text.p: Sportmart Inc said Thursday it will incur a fourth-quarter charge of $18 million to $21 million, after related income tax benefits, to close all of its Canadian operations.
The retailer, citing lower than expected U.S. sales in November and December, also estimated that total sales for the fourth quarter will be about $139 million to $141 million.
Based on these sales estimates, it said it expects to report a consolidated loss for both the fourth quarter and year ending February 2, 1997, before non-recurring charges.
Through its Canadian move, Sportmart said it expects to avoid a projected net loss of about $3.5 million to $4.5 million during fiscal 1997, which ends February 2, 1998.
The company said it engaged Hilco/Great American Group to begin immediately liquidating the Canadian inventories, which should be completed by the end of the company's fiscal first quarter.
For the nine months ended October 27, 1996, the company reported a profit of $1.5 million, or $0.12 per share, before extraordinary items.
The $0.12 per share profit represents a $0.40 per share profit for U.S. operations and a $0.28 per share loss for Canadian operations.
Sportmart will close its Canadian operations to focus on the core U.S. market.

Management said the significant sales decline in the Canadian stores stemmed largely from a dramatic increase in the number of sporting goods superstores in Canada over the past two years coupled with declining demand in the Canadian sporting goods market during 1996.
"In addition to the disappointing sales in Canada, the November and December sales in the U.S. were also below expectations," Sportmart president Mark Scott said in a statement.

"Continued soft sales in hard-goods, except golf, and an unexpected decline in fitness business had an adverse affect on our comparable store sales performance in the U.S. In addition, we did not repeat two clearance promotions during the quarter which negatively affected comparable store sales more than anticipated but positively impacted merchandise margin," he said.
Sportmart expects to report fourth quarter and year-end results in late March.
